def is_arithmetic_progression(seq):
    if len(seq) <= 2:
        return True

    # Calculate the difference of the first two elements
    diff = seq[1] - seq[0]
    
    # Check if each consecutive pair of elements has the same difference
    for i in range(2, len(seq)):
        if seq[i] - seq[i - 1] != diff:
            return False
    
    return True

def find_arithmetic_progression_index(n, b):
    b.sort()
    
    # Check if the original sequence is already an arithmetic progression
    if n == 1:
        return 1  # Any single element can form an arithmetic progression
    
    # Calculate potential common difference
    common_difference = b[1] - b[0]
    
    # Check for the case when the sequence is almost an AP, missing one element
    if n == 2:
        if common_difference == 0:
            return 1  # If there are duplicates
        else:
            return 1 if b[1] + common_difference == b[0] else 2

    # Check if deleting one element can result in an arithmetic progression
    for j in range(n):
        # Simulate removing element j
        remaining = b[:j] + b[j+1:]
        
        # Calculate differences between consecutive elements
        differences = [remaining[i] - remaining[i - 1] for i in range(1, len(remaining))]
        
        # Check if all differences are equal
        if all(d == differences[0] for d in differences):
            return j + 1  # Convert 0-based index to 1-based

    return -1

        if is_ap_new:
            return j + 1

    b.sort()

            is_ap = False
            break

    # Try removing each element and see if the remaining form an AP

                is_ap = False
                break
        
        if is_ap:
            return j + 1  # Return 1-based index

    return -1
